prompt: Which of these was not part of the modern atomic theory as John Dalton stated it in 1808?

choices.text: Atoms are made of protons, neutrons, and electrons
All matter is composed of atoms
choices.why: This is the first part of Dalton's theory.

choices.text: Atoms of the same element are the same; atoms of different elements are different
choices.why: This is the second part of Dalton's theory.

choices.text: Atoms combine in whole-number ratios to form compounds
choices.why: This is the third part of Dalton's theory.

explanation: Dalton's theory has three parts: all matter is composed of atoms, atoms of the same element are the same, and atoms combine in whole-number ratios. The subatomic particles were discovered later: first the electron, then the proton and the neutron.

prompt: Using Table 3.2.1, about how many electrons together have the same mass as one proton?
explanation: Divide the masses: (1.6 × 10^−27 kg)/(9.1 × 10^−31 kg) ≈ 1,800, or 1.8 × 10^3. Electrons are so light that almost all of an atom's mass is in its nucleus, with the protons and neutrons.

prompt: An atom has 19 protons, 20 neutrons, and 19 electrons. What is its mass number?
explanation: The mass number counts only the particles in the nucleus: 19 protons + 20 neutrons = 39. Electrons aren't included.

prompt: Which pair of atoms are isotopes of the same element?

choices.text: One with 8 protons and 8 neutrons, and one with 8 protons and 10 neutrons
One with 6 protons and 6 neutrons, and one with 7 protons and 6 neutrons
choices.why: Different numbers of protons mean different elements: these are a carbon atom and a nitrogen atom.

choices.text: One with 6 protons and 8 neutrons, and one with 7 protons and 7 neutrons
choices.why: Both have a mass number of 14, but they have different numbers of protons, so they are different elements. Isotopes share the number of protons, not the mass number.

explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element, so they have the same number of protons, with different numbers of neutrons. Both of these atoms have 8 protons (oxygen), with 8 and 10 neutrons.

prompt: How many neutrons are in an atom of chlorine-37? Chlorine's atomic number is 17.
explanation: The 37 in chlorine-37 is the mass number: protons plus neutrons. The atomic number, 17, is the number of protons, so the atom has 37 − 17 = 20 neutrons.

prompt: Which symbol represents an atom with 15 protons and 16 neutrons?

choices.why: The top number is the mass number: protons plus neutrons, 15 + 16 = 31, not just the neutrons.
The bottom number is the atomic number, the number of protons: 15, not the 16 neutrons. An atomic number of 15 means phosphorus.
The numbers are swapped: the mass number goes on top and the atomic number on the bottom.

explanation: In an isotope's symbol, the top number is the mass number (15 + 16 = 31) and the bottom number is the atomic number (15). The element with atomic number 15 is phosphorus, P.

prompt: How many electrons are in a neutral atom of ⁵⁹₂₇Co?
explanation: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons. The atomic number, 27, is the number of protons, so the atom has 27 electrons. (59 is the mass number, and 59 − 27 = 32 is the number of neutrons.)
